On this day in History: 
On December 11, 1972, Apollo 17 began NASA’s final Apollo mission—the last time humans walked on the Moon. Commander Gene Cernan, geologist Harrison Schmitt, and Ronald Evans touched down at 19:54:58 UTC, marking the end of an extraordinary era.

Apollo 17 set multiple records: the first scientist on the Moon, the longest crewed lunar mission (12 days, 14 hours), the farthest lunar EVAs (7.6 km / 4.7 miles), the most time on the surface, and 75 lunar orbits.

Visit the Aerospace Museum of California to explore our exhibit honoring all Apollo missions and the legacy of human lunar exploration. | Aerospace Museum of California | Facebook
